Data Sourcing and Generation Steps:

1. CLONE / SYNC THE ORE ENGINE SOURCE
   Source: OreStudio's fork of the ORE Engine, kept in sync with
   upstream OpenSourceRisk/Engine (this replaces the previous
   "download OreStudio/OreStudio's own zip" instructions below, which
   were stale/incorrect -- that repo is this one, it never contained
   ORE's Examples/xsd; the actual, correct source has always been
   manifest.json's own source_url, OpenSourceRisk/Engine, now tracked
   via OreStudio's own fork so local hand-patches/version pins are
   possible without forking on every refresh).
     git@github.com:OreStudio/Engine.git    (fork, push target)
     git@github.com:OpenSourceRisk/Engine.git   (upstream, pull-only)
   Kept as a separate checkout OUTSIDE this repo (e.g.
   ~/Development/ORE/Engine), not a submodule.
   Commands (first time):
     git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:OreStudio/Engine.git
     cd Engine
     git remote add upstream git@github.com:OpenSourceRisk/Engine.git
   Commands (updating the fork before syncing):
     git fetch upstream
     git checkout master && git merge --ff-only upstream/master
     git submodule update --init --recursive
     git push origin master

2. SYNC EXAMPLES + XSD
   Script: external/ore/tools/update_ore_samples.sh
   Command:
     ./external/ore/tools/update_ore_samples.sh <path-to-ore-engine-checkout>
   Target: external/ore/examples/ (+ its own manifest.json) and
   external/ore/xsd/ (+ its own manifest.json), synced together from the
   same engine commit -- a schema/example version mismatch produces
   spurious validation failures unrelated to either side being wrong.
   Validates every example XML against the freshly synced schema
   automatically (scripts/validate_ore_examples.sh) before finishing.
   See external/ore/examples/methodology.txt and
   external/ore/xsd/README.md for the full detail on what gets
   vendored/excluded.

   KNOWN HAND-PATCHES (reapplied automatically by this script -- do not
   remove without re-verifying against upstream first): 3 files ship a
   genuinely wrong FX/RATE key order from upstream (confirmed against
   QuantLib's own FXSpotQuote convention, not an ORE-Studio-specific
   issue -- see update_ore_samples.sh's own header comment for the
   full explanation and doc/agile/product_backlog/deferred/
   document_ore_vendor_hand_patches.org for the history/PR #1423). If a
   future upstream release fixes this at the source, the script's
   sed patch becomes a no-op (harmless) until explicitly removed once
   confirmed unnecessary.

3. PACKAGE THE ENGINE BINARY
   Script: external/ore/tools/package_ore.sh
   Command:
     ./external/ore/tools/package_ore.sh <path-to-ore-engine-build-dir>
   Target: external/ore/packages/ore-<version>-x64-linux.tar.gz (+
   diff-report.txt + this directory's own manifest.json). See
   external/ore/packages/methodology.txt for the full build/package/
   verify/install detail -- this step needs the engine actually built
   first (cmake --preset + cmake --build against the same checkout
   step 1 produced), not just the source sync from step 2.

4. CODE GENERATION
   Regenerate C++ domain types from the (freshly synced) XSD schemas
   using xsdcpp:
     ./projects/ores.codegen/scripts/xsdcpp_generate_ore.sh
   Requires xsdcpp on PATH. If built locally, prepend to PATH:
     PATH="/path/to/xsdcpp/build/src:$PATH" ./projects/ores.codegen/scripts/xsdcpp_generate_ore.sh
   This regenerates:
     - projects/ores.ore/include/ores.ore/domain/domain.hpp
     - projects/ores.ore/src/domain/domain.cpp
   Run this whenever step 2 changes external/ore/xsd/ content, even if
   examples/ alone changed and packages/ didn't move -- the generated
   domain types are schema-derived, not example-derived.

5. COMMIT TO REPOSITORY
   git add external/ore/* projects/ores.ore/include/ores.ore/domain/domain.hpp projects/ores.ore/src/domain/domain.cpp
   git commit -m "[data] Update ORE Sample Data"
   Commit examples/, xsd/, packages/, and the regenerated domain.hpp/
   domain.cpp together -- they're all derived from the same engine
   commit and should never land out of step with each other.
